title: Gapless streaming metering: snapshot protocol to harmonize tokenizer drift and reconnects
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Token count divergence occurs between client-side tokenizers and our server canonical tokenizer across long-lived streaming sessions, reconnects, speculative preemptions, and when attachments or encoding changes are present. These divergences lead to incorrect billing, customer disputes, and audit failures.

Goal: Design and implement a gapless streaming snapshot protocol plus reconciliation pass that ensures final billed token counts are canonical, idempotent, and reconcilable even when fragments arrive out-of-order, clients switch tokenizers, or streams reconnect mid-generation. The protocol must be efficient (low extra RPC payload), backward compatible with existing streaming clients where possible, and safe for multi-tenant billing ledgers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Finalized sessions must have a canonical token count that matches server-side tokenizer normalization for >= 99.99% of sessions in the synthetic test harness (target: <0.01% divergence).
2) Checkpoints/ snapshots are idempotent (replay-safe) and do not create duplicate ledger entries under reconnect/retry scenarios.
3) Retroactive credit/correction flow emits an audit event and corrects billed totals within SLA window for detected mismatches.
4) End-to-end integration tests for multipart attachments, UTF-8 edge cases, and tokenizer-upgrade toggles pass in CI with no flaky runs due to ordering.
5) No measurable increase (>5%) in median 95th percentile tokenization latency on streaming hot paths after opt-in telemetry is enabled.
technical_notes: Design sketch: introduce a lightweight snapshot message (stream_checkpoint) that contains: monotonic session_sequence, client_token_offset (bytes), server_token_offset_hint, short provenance_hash (sha1 of last 512 bytes), and optional diff blob when client-side pretokenization differs from server canonicalizer.

Server behavior: on receipt of a checkpoint, persist an idempotent checkpoint record (session_id + sequence) and compute a reconciliation hint by running canonical tokenizer on the near-prefix. If divergence is detected beyond heuristics, mark session as "needs_reconcile" and schedule a reconciliation pass at finalization or lower-priority background worker.

Billing ledger changes: checkpoint entries create provisional ledger markers (not final debits). Final debits occur only at session finalization after reconciliation. Add ability to issue retro-credit transactions with audit reason codes when reconciliations change billed totals.
Rate limiting: snapshot messages should be rate-limited per session to avoid churn on hot clients. Use burst tokens (max 5 checkpoints/min) and a lightweight QPS guard to protect DB write throughput.

Backward compatibility: clients not sending checkpoints will fall back to existing heuristics. Server will attempt to canonicalize at finalization but may produce larger reconciling diffs; document behavior in SDK changelog.

DB schema (high level): add table session_checkpoints(session_id, sequence, client_offset_bytes, server_hint_tokens, provenance_hash, status, created_at). All fields are opaque strings or integers at storage layer; migration to compressed storage will be handled in later PR.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API + proto design; review with API and SDK owners; draft Confluence proposal and small compatibility matrix (Aisha).
Week 2: Server checkpoint ingest path + idempotency (Marco) + DB migrations (one migration adding session_checkpoints).
Week 3: Reconciliation worker implementation and ledger provisional markers (billing infra collaboration).

Week 4: Integration tests (synthetic harness covering reconnects, tokenizer toggles, multipart attachments) and e2e metering audit run on staging; add dashboard metrics (mismatch_rate, reconcile_queue_latency, retro_credit_rate).
Week 5: Canary rollout behind feature flag; run canary on 5% of traffic and monitor mismatch signal for two weeks. Prepare rollback and retro-credit throttling configs.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Draft ticket created and initial design posted to /confluence/metering/gapless-snapshot-protocol. Assigned to Marco Li.
2026-03-11: Design review with billing infra and SDK owners. Action: tighten provenance_hash to 256-bit truncated blake2b; add max-checkpoint-size 2kb. (Decision recorded in design doc)

2026-03-12: DB migration skeleton and proto v1 committed to github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/4321. Added ENG-314159 and ENG-314271 as referenced ledger and sparse-chunk tickets for dependency mapping.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: checkpoints are provisional and final billing happens only after canonicalization to avoid double-charging. Expect multiple follow-ups: (1) SDK ergonomic convenience for checkpoint coalescing, (2) compact on-wire diff format, (3) audit tooling to explain retro-credits to customers. Also coordinate with the console team to surface reconciliation statuses in per-route dashboards.
